global_conventions: In the Stacks Project, rings are commutative and unital unless explicitly otherwise stated, zero ring permitted; modules unitary. These are terminology conventions not extra theorem-specific assumptions.

section_context_leads.content: Coherent sheaf equals finite type quasi-coherent sheaf on a Noetherian scheme; quasi-coherent subquotients of coherent sheaves are coherent; supports of coherent sheaves are closed.
section_context_leads.note: The introduction considers a Noetherian X for examples. A candidate without an explicit X-hypothesis still needs independent assessment; do not retroactively impose X Noetherian on every lemma.

section_context_leads.scope: s12 and named Coh(X,I) references afterwards
section_context_leads.content: For a Noetherian scheme X and quasi-coherent ideal sheaf I, Coh(X,I) is the category of inverse systems (F_n) of coherent O_X-modules, each annihilated by I^n, with transition-induced isomorphisms F_{n+1}/I^n F_{n+1} ≅ F_n.
section_context_leads.note: A candidate using Coh(X,I) must state X Noetherian and I quasi-coherent, unless the theorem itself fixes them; some references to the completion functor still require expansion.

section_context_leads.content: Scheme-theoretic associated points correspond most directly to affine associated primes under local Noetherian/finite type assumptions; the author warns about weaker general hypotheses.
section_context_leads.note: Do not make X Noetherian for the entire section; individual lemmas state their own restrictions.

section_context_leads.content: Relative assassin behaves most conveniently when fibres are locally Noetherian; the source expressly warns that general cases differ.
section_context_leads.note: Do not import local Noetherianity of fibres unconditionally.

section_context_leads.scope: Norms section and later linked use
section_context_leads.content: For a finite morphism π:X→Y and integer d≥1, a norm of degree d consists of a multiplicative map Norm_π:π_*O_X→O_Y of sheaves, restricting to g↦g^d on O_Y, and satisfying the stated vanishing condition for functions vanishing at points above y.
section_context_leads.note: The source explicitly distinguishes norm property (1) from extra vanishing property (2) and indicates some constructions only need (1). Do not silently require a norm in theorems whose conclusion constructs it.

section_context_leads.content: Conormal algebra C_{Z/X,*}=⊕_{n≥0} I^n/I^{n+1}; grade n C_{Z/X,n}; canonical Sym(C_{Z/X})→C_{Z/X,*}.
section_context_leads.note: Initial Z→X immersion in explanatory prose is schematic; the candidate's own immersion supplies actual variables.

section_context_leads.content: Regularity conditions on the ideal sheaf representing an immersion are independent of the chosen open neighborhood where it becomes a closed immersion.
section_context_leads.note: Do not carry specific U or I from expository paragraph into a lemma.

section_context_leads.content: Introduces following lemmas concerning pullbacks of regular meromorphic sections.
section_context_leads.note: Local scheme maps and their meromorphic pullback conditions remain theorem-specific.
